subject.title: fix(azure): responses model aliases route correctly

question: Is the PR's OpenClaw CLI probe against a local Azure Responses-compatible mock server sufficient proof for this resolver-layer auth-provider routing fix, or must the contributor provide a live Azure credential probe before merge?
rationale: The code path being fixed is local provider/model owner selection, but repository policy treats external API/auth-provider work as proof-sensitive and the PR intentionally lacks live Azure credentials.

options.title: Accept resolver-level proof
options.body: Accept the mock Responses probe plus focused resolver tests as sufficient because the Azure-specific claim is that OpenClaw chooses the Azure provider, URL shape, and api-key header before the network call.

options.title: Require live Azure proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted live Azure `models status --probe` or agent smoke before merge if maintainers want end-to-end credential validation rather than resolver proof.

options.title: Pause for owner-boundary review
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers want a different permanent boundary between manifest alias canonicalization and provider runtime hooks.

recommendation.title: Accept resolver-level proof
recommendation.body: Accept the mock Responses probe plus focused resolver tests as sufficient because the Azure-specific claim is that OpenClaw chooses the Azure provider, URL shape, and api-key header before the network call.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is about OpenAI/Azure catalog and proof expectations, and steipete has recent OpenAI catalog ownership signals in the affected manifest surface.
